evidence_limits: All motion is genuine recording source 13, at its original 20 fps and original speed. Titles/captions, opaque privacy masks, integer cropping and unscaled padding are editorial changes. No obscured UI was reconstructed, no screenshot was inserted as motion, and no original wait inside an archive section was shortened.

The archive retains continuous safe sections rather than only highlight moments. Every temporal omission is listed. It also retains 29.10 seconds of elapsed time behind a complete opaque UI mask during moving private Logs identifiers; these visibility removals are listed separately and are not presented as visible product evidence.

The browser error 9 interval from raw 5914.55 to 6032.05 seconds lasts 117.50 seconds and is retained as an explicitly labeled browser/tooling interruption. It is not classified as a Datadog evaluation error or product defect.

The expired session is visibly resumed, receives new events, and is then stopped. Retained history remains available. Source clocks identify observed frames; displayed event rows are not automatically the exact execution time of the selected capture.

Incomplete and non-Boolean conditions are visibly marked invalid; a correction is followed by VALID2 quantity=2 rows. Missing-local evaluation feedback names the expression and provides edit guidance. The definedness expression subsequently renders missing=False. These are specific observed validation/recovery behaviors, not new defect claims.

With variable capture off, the selected message-only event explains that it lacks debugging information. Re-enabling capture produces guidance about future events while the older event remains OUTDATED; a subsequent selected event includes locals. The MESSAGE_ONLY prefix is a user-written template and remains after capture is re-enabled.

Function captures expose Values on exit and @return. Later, the function @return expression renders a returned dictionary, while a line logpoint reports No such local variable for @return. The highlight omits a long preceding historical-view wait, so it must not be used to claim immediate event delivery after Apply.

Complex, nested, cyclic and Unicode fixture interactions are real recorded UI. Some lowest rows are clipped and some values/source are privacy-masked. The excerpts do not establish unbounded cycle behavior, a universal depth/string limit, shared-object identity, or a data-corruption defect.

Targeted redaction is demonstrated with synthetic fields: ordinary controls remain visible, and expansion explains that sensitive-name values were redacted based on their names. Source literals resembling secrets are conservatively hidden in the archive. No actual credential is published.

The sampled concurrent examples are sample A from pair 41 with side=101, quantity=2, total=2400, and sample B from pair 53 with side=202, quantity=4, total=4320. They are different sampled pairs, not the two members of one demonstrated concurrent pair. A/B here describe synthetic sides and do not denote repository permission scope.

Actual Trace views show GET /qa and SPAN WITH LOG for the sampled events, with displayed durations of 729 and 887 microseconds. Runtime, repository, process, span and trace identifiers are masked. The event-heading times are preserved as UI text and are not substituted for independently verified snapshot execution timestamps.

Caught-exception, optional/deleted-local and assigned-branch controls are visible. Displayed null values alone do not establish how absent and deleted variables are represented in the indexed payload.

The foreground recording shows the TAB_A2 quantity == 3 draft and blue Apply styling, then separate later TAB_A3 rows. It does not visibly expose the complete editor before/after state used to confirm the unsaved-draft loss. That confirmation relies on separately reviewed stills and run observations, which are not reconstructed into this video.

A DISABLED-to-INSTRUMENTING status change is visible after an update sequence, but the stale-edit reactivation mechanism remains unconfirmed by this evidence. Captions distinguish the observed status from a causal defect claim.

Lifecycle excerpts preserve state-specific header masks and show an inactive parent with visible disabled children, followed by child activation, an active parent and the chosen child receiving events while visible siblings remain disabled. Only visible rows are claimed; an individual frame does not enumerate every child.

Cancel/refresh typing is only partly exposed in foreground motion. Historical-range and ascending-sort states are visible. The final inventory shows All 4, Active 0 and Inactive 4, with all four visible cards marked INACTIVE.

UTC caption ranges are reconstructed from the recorder start. Datadog event lists use a displayed UTC-07:00 offset. Recording clocks, UI row/header timestamps, observer timestamps and snapshot execution timestamps are distinct evidence types.

Browser chrome, private URLs, account/profile/session/runtime/trace identifiers, repository prefixes and synthetic correlation identifier strings are cropped, masked or omitted. Conservative source/value masks also hide adjacent ordinary content. Numeric synthetic pair/side indices remain where needed for the demonstrated controls.

Earlier frozen media remain unchanged. Public folders contain only sanitized MP4s, public manifests, readable maps and checksums; no raw recording, internal journal, diagnostic contact sheet or build script is included.
